source.title: Towards Understanding the Generalization Bias of Two Layer Convolutional Linear Classifiers with Gradient Descent
source.authors: Yi-Fan Wu; B. Póczos; Aarti Singh

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper; no garbling or cutoff is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: Compares convolutional and single-layer linear classifiers under gradient descent on three synthetic 1D tasks, testing the architectural generalization advantage with a different setting from the image-classification conditions in V3.
record.gate_note: The paper explicitly reports the architecture comparison in Figure 2. Random-label behavior is discussed as a cited finding or a stated consequence of independently flipped labels, not reported as a new experiment. Figure 5’s loss comparisons do not isolate the architecture effect and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests V3's architecture comparison in a new setting: synthetic one-dimensional images classified by linear convolutional and fully connected networks trained with gradient descent. It reports an accuracy advantage despite identical represented function classes.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors explain a convolutional generalization advantage on spatially structured synthetic tasks through the interaction of architecture, data and gradient descent. Their analysis uses asymptotic X-hinge dynamics as a surrogate for ordinary hinge training, and shows that the useful bias can require enough training samples to emerge.
record.recipe_differences: Uses single-filter, two-layer convolutional linear classifiers and synthetic 1D tasks; compares against single-layer linear classifiers with full-batch gradient descent and hinge loss.
record.method_sensitivity: Task and training sample count; the paper reports similar performance at small sample counts on Task-Cls and an advantage as the count grows.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors argue that training-loss sharpness contains no information about unseen coordinates in Task-Cls.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-loss sharpness need not determine generalization on sparse synthetic linear classification tasks.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics 2019 (PMLR Volume 89)
record.problems: The experiments use simplified synthetic 1D tasks, not image datasets. Figure 2 provides plotted results without numerical values or uncertainty estimates in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 5 and later figures compare hinge-loss variants, asymptotic analysis, and initialization effects within the convolutional model; these do not isolate the architecture comparison named in V3.

untested.parts: Joint measurement of random-label fitting, natural-label generalization and chance performance on unseen random labels.
Width sweeps beyond the width required to interpolate.

The named natural-image benchmarks; nonlinear deep networks; isolation of local connectivity from weight sharing; fully connected networks learning sparse local connections or initialized from trained convolutional networks.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and effects of tuning.
Batch-size penalties under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout and its interactions with dataset size, augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness rankings of generalization gaps within a convolutional family and comparisons against other measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

missing.what: Convolutional versus single-layer accuracy on the odd/even-position classification task, with alternating-sign learned filters.
The reported two-layer fully connected comparator has the same generalization behavior as the single-layer classifier in all experiments; no separate curves or numerical values are supplied.

Theoretical qualification: for Task-Cls under asymptotic X-hinge dynamics, training positions at least k and separated by at least 2k yield no convolutional generalization advantage under Gaussian filter initialization.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for V3. Its synthetic one-dimensional images provide a restricted new setting. Equal function classes rule out reduced representational capacity as the explanation, but do not isolate local connectivity from weight sharing. Proposition 6 concerns asymptotic X-hinge dynamics and should not be presented as a direct empirical failure under ordinary hinge training.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
No network-width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
Image datasets and fully connected networks learning sparse local connections or initialized from trained convolutional networks.
Magnitude-aware sharpness or comparisons with other generalization measures.
Removal of memorized examples and retraining.
